title: Best AI Mandarin Speaking Apps Ranked for 2026
summary: Compare AI apps for learning Mandarin speaking in November 2026, including pricing, tone handling, and practice style.
body_markdown:
Mandarin learners have a specific problem: plenty of tools for characters and HSK decks, almost nothing that pushes you to speak until the tones stop tripping you up. That's the gap we're looking at today. Below are the AI apps doing the best job of getting you talking, with straight notes on where each one falls short.


**TLDR:**


- Mandarin punishes passive study because four tones, pinyin-to-sound mapping, and measure words only automate through spoken reps under pressure
- Push-to-talk voice interaction breaks conversational rhythm; smart turn detection is the dividing line between most apps reviewed and natural practice
- HelloChinese handles pinyin, tones, and character work for beginners; Speak offers scripted scenarios; ChatGPT works as a flexible but unguided partner
- Verify free-trial status, pricing, and web availability on each competitor's live site before subscribing, since features shift often
- ISSEN is a real-time AI voice tutor with cross-session memory, conversation-anchored SRS flashcards, and a separate Shadowing mode for tone drills


## What is an AI app for learning Mandarin Chinese speaking


An AI app for learning Mandarin Chinese speaking uses voice AI to simulate real conversation, respond to what you say, and build the productive side of fluency that textbooks and flashcards never quite reach. These apps sit in a different category from the best apps to learn Mandarin for reading or character writing. Their job is spoken output.


The focus matters because Mandarin punishes passive study. Four tones change the meaning of a syllable entirely, pinyin has to map cleanly to sound before it maps to characters, and structures like measure words and aspect particles (了) only become automatic through repeated use under conversational pressure.


[AI speaking practice](https://www.issen.com/blog/how-ai-speaking-practice-works/) pushes you to produce Mandarin out loud, holds the conversation at a level you can mostly follow, and surfaces the patterns you keep missing. Character drills, HSK decks, and grammar explainers belong alongside it as separate study tracks.


## How we ranked the best AI apps for learning Mandarin


Our rankings draw on publicly available information: each app's website, App Store listings, and published feature documentation as of November 2026. We did not run controlled proprietary tests, and pricing, free-trial status, and features can shift. Verify specifics on the live site before paying.


The criteria we weighed:


- Real-time voice conversation quality, including whether the app supports natural turn-taking or relies on push-to-talk.
- Mandarin-specific support: tone handling, pinyin display, and simplified or traditional character options.
- Curriculum adaptability to your level, interests, and pace.
- Accent coverage across Mainland and Taiwanese Mandarin.
- Pricing model, favoring flat monthly rates over per-session fees.
- Availability across iOS, Android, and web, with cross-device sync.


Where a competitor claim could not be confirmed on the live listing, we flagged it instead of guessing.


## Best Overall AI App for Learning Mandarin Chinese: ISSEN


ISSEN is a real-time AI voice tutor built around conversation, with support for 60+ languages including Mandarin Chinese. The tutor drives the conversation, adapts vocabulary and pace to your level, and remembers your interests across sessions so you are not re-explaining who you are every time you open the app.


For Mandarin, that means full conversations from session one, flashcards tied to sentences you actually spoke, and pronunciation work handed off to a separate Shadowing mode for structured drills.


Core strengths:


- Real-time voice conversation with smart turn detection, no push-to-talk.
- Cross-session memory for your interests, goals, and recurring stumbles.
- Background mode for hands-free practice while walking or commuting.
- Conversation-anchored SRS flashcards pulled from your own spoken sentences.
- Dedicated Shadowing mode for pronunciation drills, separate from conversation.
- Available on iOS, Android, and web with instant sync across devices.
- 10-minute free trial.
- Flat monthly pricing from $20 to $29 USD depending on plan and country.


**Bottom line:** ISSEN is the best choice for learners who want to speak Mandarin with confidence by accumulating real conversation volume rather than tapping through gamified drills.


Try ISSEN free for 10 minutes.


## Speak


Speak, built by Speakeasy Labs, is an AI speaking practice app that includes Mandarin Chinese, structured around short video explanations, scripted roleplay scenarios, and feedback on target phrases. The app is mobile-first on iOS and Android.


### What they offer


- Structured curriculum lessons with video explanations
- AI roleplay scenarios for scripted practice
- Pronunciation feedback on target phrases
- Mobile-first with iOS and Android support


**Good for:** Beginners who want a scenario-based lesson path with scripted speaking drills.


**Where it falls short:** Conversation practice is primarily scripted instead of open-ended. No dedicated shadowing mode or conversation-anchored SRS tied to the learner's own sentences. Verify free trial status on the[live App Store listing](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/speak-language-learning/id1286609883) before subscribing.


**Bottom line:** Speak suits Mandarin beginners wanting short structured drills; ISSEN fits learners who need open-ended Mandarin conversation reps.


## Praktika


Praktika is an AI language tutor app built around lifelike avatar characters that act as video-style tutors. It supports 11 languages including Mandarin Chinese, a count that treats Brazilian and European Portuguese as separate entries, as listed on its[current App Store catalog summary](https://www.chickytutor.com/blog/vs-praktika) .


### What they offer


- Avatar-based video-style tutors for speaking practice
- 1,000+ lessons spanning travel scenarios and structured learning paths
- Pronunciation feedback and personalized study plans


Good for: Learners who respond to visual avatar tutors and want structured lesson scaffolding.


Where it falls short: Among the[language learning apps with AI voice](https://www.issen.com/blog/ai-language-learning-apps-voice-practice/) , Praktika uses push-to-talk mechanics instead of smart turn detection, so you tap to speak instead of flowing through natural turns. It lacks background mode for hands-free practice and does not offer conversation-anchored SRS flashcards pulled from your own spoken sentences.


Bottom line: Praktika fits learners who want avatar-led structure, but ISSEN is better for building daily conversational volume in Mandarin.


## Talkpal


Talkpal is an AI language app that pairs text chat with optional voice features across a wide language catalog, including Mandarin Chinese, and sits among several[AI apps for real conversation practice](https://www.issen.com/blog/best-ai-apps-practicing-language-real-conversations/) . It runs on mobile and web.


### What they offer


- AI chat and voice conversations across many languages
- Roleplay scenarios for scripted practice contexts
- Grammar explanations tied to chat exchanges
- Mobile and web availability


Good for: Learners who prefer a text-heavy AI chat experience with voice as an optional layer.


Where it falls short: Talkpal uses push-to-talk voice interaction instead of smart turn detection, which breaks conversational rhythm. It lacks a dedicated shadowing mode, cross-session memory of prior struggles, and a hands-free background mode.


Bottom line: Talkpal fits chat-first learners, but ISSEN is better for voice-first Mandarin practice.


## HelloChinese


HelloChinese is a Mandarin-specific app built around gamified lessons covering pinyin, tones, characters, and foundational grammar. Its narrow focus on Mandarin gives it more depth on character work and tone drills than generic apps.


### What they offer


- Gamified lesson sequences covering pinyin, tones, and grammar
- Simplified character writing practice
- Listening and reading exercises tied to lesson vocabulary
- Pronunciation checks on short target phrases


Good for: Absolute beginners building Mandarin vocabulary and character recognition from zero.


Where it falls short: No open-ended spoken dialogue, no cross-session memory, and no conversation-anchored SRS pulled from sentences you actually produced.


Bottom line: HelloChinese works for early vocabulary and character work; ISSEN takes over once you need to speak.


## ChatGPT


ChatGPT is OpenAI's general-purpose AI chat tool with a voice mode that some Mandarin learners repurpose as an informal speaking partner. The tool is flexible and already in many learners' pockets, which makes it a convenient starting point even though it was never built for language teaching.


### What they offer


- Voice conversations in Mandarin through the mobile app's voice mode
- Grammar explanations and on-demand translations between English and Mandarin
- Flexible open-ended prompts you can shape to any topic
- Availability across web, iOS, and Android


Good for: Self-directed learners who already have a study plan and want a conversation partner for occasional practice.


Limitation: ChatGPT waits for you to lead, so it does not drive the conversation, set a curriculum, track progress across sessions, adjust difficulty to your CEFR level, or surface vocabulary from prior sessions as reviewable flashcards.


Bottom line: ChatGPT works as a flexible conversation partner for Mandarin, but ISSEN is the better choice for learners who want a tutor that actually steers the practice.

Mandarin speakers get the most from ISSEN, one of the[best language learning apps for speaking](https://www.issen.com/blog/best-language-learning-apps-speaking/) , because the product is built around the parts of Chinese that only yield to spoken repetition: real-time voice conversation without push-to-talk, cross-session memory that tracks which tones and structures you keep slipping on, conversation-anchored SRS pulled from sentences you actually said, a dedicated Shadowing mode for tone drills across native accents, and background mode for hands-free reps during commutes, the same features that make ISSEN rank among the[best AI apps for English speaking practice](https://www.issen.com/blog/best-ai-apps-for-learning-english-speaking/) .


The gap between understanding Mandarin and speaking it closes through daily conversational practice. Flashcards and grammar notes support that practice without replacing it. Start a 10-minute conversation with ISSEN and let your next real exchange in Chinese feel less terrifying than the last.


## Final thoughts on finding the right Chinese speaking app


Every app on this list does something useful, but the one that moves your Mandarin forward is the one that gets you speaking out loud every day. Match your choice to how you actually practice rather than to the feature list that looks best on paper.[Open ISSEN and talk for 10 minutes](https://www.issen.com/) to see what daily voice reps feel like.


## FAQ


### How do I pick between ISSEN, Speak, Praktika, Talkpal, HelloChinese, and ChatGPT for Mandarin?


Start with what you need to build: if you need characters and foundational vocabulary, HelloChinese is the right starting point; if you need scripted scenario drills, Speak fits; if you need open-ended voice conversation reps at the intermediate level and above, ISSEN is the better match. ChatGPT works as a flexible partner when you already have a study plan and only need someone to talk to.


### Is HelloChinese better than ISSEN for a complete beginner learning Mandarin?


For the first few months, yes. HelloChinese covers pinyin, tones, and character recognition in a structured sequence that ISSEN does not replicate. Once you can read basic sentences and want to produce spoken Mandarin under real conversational pressure, ISSEN takes over as the speaking layer.


### Can ISSEN give me pronunciation feedback on my tones during a Mandarin conversation?


Tone and pronunciation work happens in ISSEN's dedicated Shadowing mode, which runs pause-and-repeat drills separately from voice conversations. Conversation sessions build fluency and spoken volume; Shadowing handles the structured pronunciation reps for the four Mandarin tones.


### Is ChatGPT good enough for Mandarin speaking practice if I already pay for it?


ChatGPT's voice mode works as a conversation partner, but it waits for you to lead, has no curriculum, no cross-session memory of what you keep missing, and no vocabulary surfaced from your actual spoken sentences. For occasional practice that's fine; for a daily tutor that steers the session and tracks your gaps, a product built for teaching does more useful work per minute.


### How much daily practice do I actually need to build Mandarin speaking confidence?


The[FSI language difficulty rankings](https://www.state.gov/foreign-language-training/) classify Mandarin as a Category IV language, estimating around 2,200 classroom hours for working proficiency for English speakers, so expect a multi-year horizon. A realistic daily target is 15 to 30 minutes of spoken output. Consistency beats intensity here: showing up every day for a short session builds the tone recall and sentence patterns that twice-a-week marathons never automate.
